_readme: Committed floors for the OpenSSF Scorecard run in .github/workflows/openssf-scorecard.yml.
The gate is .harness/scripts/ci/52-validate-scorecard-regression.mjs: a run scoring below any
floor here fails the workflow, so a posture regression is a red scheduled job and a diffable
fact rather than a number inside an artifact nobody opens.
SEEDED 2026-08-08 from the run of 2026-08-04 (commit 5396cd78, Scorecard v5.5.0), whose JSON
artifact was downloaded rather than transcribed. Until then aggregate was null and the gate
failed CLOSED by design -- inventing floors is the defect GT-597 exists to remove -- so the
scheduled workflow had been red since the day after it landed, correctly, waiting for exactly
this commit.
RATCHETING: a check scoring above its floor never fails the gate; it is reported as a
suggestion. Raising a floor stays a reviewed commit, because a baseline that updates itself
cannot detect anything.
TWO FLOORS THAT DO NOT MEAN WHAT THEY LOOK LIKE:
Branch-Protection 3 measures the INSTRUMENT, not this posture. Scorecard cannot read branch
protection with the default GITHUB_TOKEN; main and develop each carry 8 required contexts
with enforce_admins true. Do not chase this number by weakening anything real.
Signed-Releases -1 means the check never reached a verdict, not that it scored zero. A -1
floor passes against a -1 observation and any real score is an improvement.
The gate was observed RED before being trusted: dropping SAST 10 -> 4 exits 1 as REGRESSED
with the aggregate delta, and deleting a check from the set exits 1 as MISSING, because a
check that stops running looks identical to one that stopped passing.
TWO DECISIONS TAKEN 2026-08-16, WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN SILENTLY APPLIED:
1. `Maintained` scored 10 against a floor of 0, and the gate suggested raising it.
NOT RAISED, on purpose. Maintained scores recent commit and release activity, and a
90-day guard/gap freeze was declared the same day (see
reference/core/control-center/adoption/guard-and-gap-freeze-2026-08-16.md) which
deliberately reduces that activity. Pinning the floor at the peak of an unusually
busy week would manufacture a red scheduled job in a month for a slowdown that was
planned. Revisit at the freeze review, 2026-11-16.
2. `Vulnerabilities` REGRESSED 8 -> 4 (7 open Dependabot alerts: 1 high, 5 moderate,
1 low). The floor is NOT lowered to accommodate it. Lowering a floor to make a real
regression green is the one move that turns this file back into decoration. The high
one is tracked as GT-691 and is genuinely blocked: js-yaml SHIPPED its fix in 5.2.2,
but @nestjs/swagger is still `latest` at 11.4.6 pinning "js-yaml": "5.2.1" exactly,
and the only newer releases are 12.0.0-alpha.*. The gate stays red until the
vulnerabilities are actually resolved, which is the gate working.
